what: Extra Space Storage is the largest self-storage operator in the United States by number of properties. It owns storage facilities and also manages them for other owners under its brand.
customers: Households moving or short of space, students, and small businesses storing stock and equipment.
money: insurance sold to tenants and fees for managing others' facilities
moat: Density in urban markets where new storage is hard to permit, and a brand that captures online searches, which is how most customers now find storage.
risks: Debt of about $10 billion against almost no cash
Demand depends on people moving house, which high mortgage rates have slowed
New supply in some markets pressures rents
opportunities: Operating margin of 42% because facilities need very few staff
Managing other owners' facilities earns fees without using capital
